translations.literal: Zhang Wenjin was a native of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenjin was a native of Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Hongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a secretary in the Bureau of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 正德初，為劉瑾所陷，逮系詔獄，斥為民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was framed by Liu Jin, arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and dismissed as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was framed by Liu Jin, arrested and imprisoned in the imperial prison, and dismissed as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，起故官。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 督稅陝西，條上籌邊裕民十事。

translations.literal: Supervising tax collection in Shaanxi, he submitted in detail ten measures for securing the border and enriching the people.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising tax collection in Shaanxi, he submitted in detail ten measures for securing the border and enriching the people.

sentences.zh: 遷安慶知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 度甯王宸濠必反，與都指揮楊銳為禦備計。

translations.literal: He judged that the Prince of Ning Chen Hao would surely rebel, and together with Regional Commander Yang Rui made preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He judged that the Prince of Ning Chen Hao would surely rebel and, together with Regional Commander Yang Rui, made preparations for defense.

sentences.zh: 宸濠果反，浮江下。

translations.literal: Chen Hao did rebel, and floated down the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao did rebel and sailed down the river.

sentences.zh: 文錦等慮其攻南都，令軍士登城詬之。

translations.literal: Wenjin and the others, fearing he would attack the Southern Capital, had soldiers mount the walls and revile him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin and the others, fearing he would attack the Southern Capital, had soldiers mount the walls and revile him.

sentences.zh: 宸濠乃留攻，卒不能克。

translations.literal: Chen Hao therefore remained to besiege and in the end could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao therefore remained to besiege the city and in the end could not take it.

sentences.zh: 事具《楊銳傳》。

translations.literal: The full account is in 《Biography of Yang Rui》.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in 《Biography of Yang Rui》.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒美，擢太僕少卿。

translations.literal: An imperial letter praised and commended him, and he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised and commended him, and he was promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，拜右副都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and grand coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 文錦性剛。

translations.literal: Wenjin's temperament was hard.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin's temperament was hard.

sentences.zh: 以拒賊得重名，遂銳意振刷，操切頗無序。

translations.literal: Because he had won a great reputation for resisting the rebels, he then sharply applied himself to reform and discipline, yet his management was rather disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had won a great reputation for resisting the rebels, he then set himself sharply to reform and discipline, yet his management was rather disorderly.

sentences.zh: 大同北四望平衍，寇至無可禦。

translations.literal: North of Datong all four directions were flat and open; when invaders arrived there was nothing with which to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: North of Datong the land was flat and open in every direction; when invaders arrived there was nothing with which to resist them.

sentences.zh: 文錦曰：「寇犯宣府不能近鎮城者，以葛谷、白陽諸堡為外蔽也。

translations.literal: Wenjin said, "When bandits invaded Xuanfu they could not approach the garrison city because fortresses such as Ge Valley and Baiyang served as outer screens."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin said, "When bandits invaded Xuanfu they could not approach the garrison city because fortresses such as Ge Valley and Baiyang served as outer screens."

sentences.zh: 今城外即戰場，何以示重？

translations.literal: "Now outside the city lies the battlefield itself—how is one to display weight and authority?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the battlefield lies right outside the city—how is one to display weight and authority?"

sentences.zh: 」議於城北九十里外，增設五堡，曰水口、宣寧、只河、柳溝、樺溝。

translations.literal: It was decided to add five fortresses ninety li north of the city, named Shuikou, Xuanning, Zhihe, Liugou, and Huagou.
translations.idiomatic: It was decided to add five fortresses ninety li north of the city, named Shuikou, Xuanning, Zhihe, Liugou, and Huagou.

sentences.zh: 參將賈鑒督役嚴，卒已怨。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Jia Jian supervised the labor strictly, and the troops were already resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Regional Commander Jia Jian supervised the labor strictly, and the troops were already resentful.

sentences.zh: 及堡成，欲徙鎮卒二千五百家戍之。

translations.literal: When the fortresses were completed, he wished to transfer twenty-five hundred garrison households of the garrison troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: When the fortresses were completed, he wished to transfer twenty-five hundred garrison households to guard them.

sentences.zh: 眾憚行，請募新丁，僚吏鹹以為言。

translations.literal: The multitude feared being sent there and requested that new recruits be hired instead; the subordinate officials all spoke on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: The men feared being sent there and requested that new recruits be hired instead; the subordinate officials all spoke on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 文錦怒曰：「如此，則令不行矣。

translations.literal: Wenjin angrily said, "If it is like this, then orders will not be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin angrily said, "If it is like this, then orders will not be carried out."

sentences.zh: 鎮親兵先往，孰敢後！

translations.literal: "The garrison's personal troops will go first—who would dare hang back!"
translations.idiomatic: "The garrison's personal troops will go first—who would dare hang back!"

sentences.zh: 」親兵素遊惰有室。

translations.literal: The personal troops had always been idle wanderers with families.
translations.idiomatic: The personal troops had always been idle and had families.

sentences.zh: 聞當發，大恐。

translations.literal: When they heard they were to be dispatched, they were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard they were to be dispatched, they were greatly alarmed.

sentences.zh: 請孑身往，得分番。

translations.literal: They requested to go alone without their families, serving in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: They requested to go alone without their families, serving in rotation.

sentences.zh: 又不聽，嚴趣之。

translations.literal: Again he would not listen, and sharply pressed them to depart.
translations.idiomatic: Again he would not listen and sharply pressed them to depart.

sentences.zh: 鑒承風，杖其隊長。

translations.literal: Jia Jian took his cue and beat their squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Jian took his cue and beat their squad leader.

sentences.zh: 諸邊卒自甘州五衛殺巡撫許銘，朝廷處之輕，頗無忌。

translations.literal: Frontier troops from the five guards of Ganzhou, who had killed Grand Coordinator Xu Ming, had been treated lightly by the court and were largely without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops from the five guards of Ganzhou, who had killed Grand Coordinator Xu Ming, had been treated lightly by the court and were largely without fear.

sentences.zh: 至是，卒郭鑒、柳忠等乘眾憤，遂倡亂。

translations.literal: At this juncture soldiers Guo Jian, Liu Zhong, and others, riding the crowd's anger, then incited the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture soldiers Guo Jian, Liu Zhong, and others, riding the crowd's anger, incited the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 殺賈鑒，裂其屍，走出塞，屯焦山墩。

translations.literal: They killed Jia Jian, tore his corpse apart, fled beyond the pass, and encamped at Jiaoshan Beacon.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Jia Jian, tore his corpse apart, fled beyond the pass, and encamped at Jiaoshan Beacon.

sentences.zh: 文錦恐與外寇連，令副將時陳等招之入城，即索治首亂者。

translations.literal: Wenjin feared they would join with foreign bandits; he ordered Vice General Shi Chen and others to lure them back into the city, and then immediately demanded punishment of the ringleaders of the disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin feared they would join with foreign bandits; he ordered Vice General Shi Chen and others to lure them back into the city and then immediately demanded punishment of the ringleaders of the mutiny.

sentences.zh: 郭鑒等大懼，復聚為亂，焚大同府門，入行都司縱獄囚，又焚都御史府門。

translations.literal: Guo Jian and the others were greatly afraid; they gathered again and made trouble, burned the gate of Datong Prefecture, entered the Regional Military Commission to release prisoners, and also burned the gate of the Censor-in-Chief's yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jian and the others were terrified. They rallied again in mutiny, burned the gate of Datong Prefecture, entered the Regional Military Commission to release prisoners, and burned the gate of the censor-in-chief's yamen as well.

sentences.zh: 文錦逾垣走，匿博野王府第。

translations.literal: Wenjin climbed over the wall and fled, hiding in the residence of the Prince of Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin climbed over the wall and fled, hiding in the residence of the Prince of Boye.

sentences.zh: 亂卒欲燔王宮。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers wished to burn the princely palace.
translations.idiomatic: The mutinous soldiers threatened to burn the princely palace.

sentences.zh: 王懼，出文錦。

translations.literal: The prince was afraid and surrendered Wenjin.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, in fear, handed Wenjin over.

sentences.zh: 郭鑒等殺之，亦裂其屍，遂焚鎮守總兵公署。

translations.literal: Guo Jian and the others killed him, also dismembered his corpse, and then burned the headquarters of the garrison commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jian and his followers killed him, dismembered his corpse, and then burned the headquarters of the garrison commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 出故總兵硃振于獄，脅為帥。

translations.literal: They released the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen from prison and coerced him to serve as leader.
translations.idiomatic: They released the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen from prison and forced him to serve as their leader.

sentences.zh: 時嘉靖三年八月也。

translations.literal: It was the eighth month of the third year of the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred in the eighth month of the third year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝命侍郎李昆赦亂卒。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Li Kun to pardon the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, the emperor ordered Vice Minister Li Kun to pardon the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 昆為文錦請恤典，不報，久之，文錦父政訟其子守安慶功，禮部為之請，終不許。

translations.literal: Kun requested posthumous honors for Wenjin, but received no reply. After a long time Wenjin's father Zheng petitioned regarding his son's merit in defending Anqing; the Ministry of Rites pleaded on his behalf, but in the end it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Kun requested posthumous honors for Wenjin, but received no reply. Long afterward, Wenjin's father Zheng petitioned regarding his son's merit in defending Anqing; the Ministry of Rites pleaded on his behalf, but the request was ultimately denied.

sentences.zh: 文錦妻李氏復上疏哀請。

translations.literal: Wenjin's wife, Lady Li, again submitted a memorial pleading in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin's wife, Lady Li, submitted another memorial pleading in grief.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命執齎疏者治之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered that the person who had delivered the memorial be seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and ordered the bearer of the memorial seized and punished.

sentences.zh: 副都御史陳洪謨言：「文錦僨事，朝廷戮之可也。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Hongmo said, "Wenjin failed in his duty; the court might execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Hongmo said, "Wenjin failed in his duty; the court could have executed him.

sentences.zh: 假手士卒，傳之四方，損國威不小。

translations.literal: But to use soldiers as one's instrument and have it spread in all directions does no small harm to national prestige."
translations.idiomatic: But to leave the deed to common soldiers and let the story spread everywhere would have done no small harm to the prestige of the state."

sentences.zh: 」復降旨詰責。

translations.literal: An edict was again issued rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was again issued rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 自是，廷臣不敢言。

translations.literal: From this time onward, court officials did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on, court officials did not dare speak out.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，始贈右都御史。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, he was at last posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, he was at last posthumously granted the title of Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追諡忠湣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 詹榮，字仁甫，山海衛人。

translations.literal: Zhan Rong, styled Renfu, was a native of Shanhai Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Rong, styled Renfu, was a native of Shanhai Guard.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，曆郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and successively served as a bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to serve as a bureau director.

sentences.zh: 督餉大同，值兵變，殺總兵官李瑾。

translations.literal: While supervising grain transport at Datong, he encountered a military mutiny in which Commander-in-Chief Li Jin was killed.
translations.idiomatic: While supervising grain transport at Datong, he encountered a military mutiny in which Commander-in-Chief Li Jin was killed.

sentences.zh: 總督劉源清率師圍城，久不下。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Liu Yuanqing led troops to besiege the city, but for a long time could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Liu Yuanqing led troops to besiege the city, but for a long time could not bring it to surrender.

sentences.zh: 榮素有智略，善應變。

translations.literal: Rong had long possessed resourcefulness and was skilled at adapting to change.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had long been known for his resourcefulness and was skilled at adapting to sudden change.

sentences.zh: 叛卒掠城中，無犯榮者。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers plundered within the city, but none harmed Rong.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel soldiers plundered the city, yet none laid a hand on Rong.

sentences.zh: 週邊益急，榮密約都指揮紀振、遊擊戴濂、鎮撫王寧同盟討賊。

translations.literal: As the situation grew more urgent, Rong secretly arranged with Regional Commander Ji Zhen, Mobile Corps Commander Dai Lian, and Garrison Pacification Commissioner Wang Ning to form an alliance to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As the crisis deepened, Rong secretly arranged with Regional Commander Ji Zhen, Mobile Corps Commander Dai Lian, and Garrison Pacification Commissioner Wang Ning to join forces against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 察叛卒馬升、楊麟無逆志，乃陽令寧持官民狀詣源清所，為叛卒乞原，而陰以榮謀告，請宥升、麟死，畀三千金，俾募死士自效。

translations.literal: Observing that the rebel soldiers Ma Sheng and Yang Lin had no rebellious intent, he outwardly ordered Ning to carry petitions from officials and commoners to Yuanqing's camp to beg pardon for the rebels, while secretly informing him of Rong's plan, requesting that Sheng and Lin be spared death, given three thousand taels of gold, and allowed to recruit daredevils to serve in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the rebel soldiers Ma Sheng and Yang Lin had no real rebellious intent, he outwardly ordered Ning to carry petitions from officials and commoners to Yuanqing's camp to beg pardon for the rebels, while secretly revealing Rong's plan: spare Sheng and Lin, give them three thousand taels of gold, and let them recruit loyal fighters to prove themselves.

sentences.zh: 會源清已罷，巡撫樊繼祖許之。

translations.literal: As it happened Yuanqing had already been dismissed, and Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu consented.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yuanqing had already been dismissed, and Grand Coordinator Fan Jizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 升、麟遂結心腹，擒首惡黃鎮等九人戮之。

translations.literal: Sheng and Lin then rallied trusted followers, seized the ringleaders Huang Zhen and eight others, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and Lin then rallied trusted followers, seized the ringleaders Huang Zhen and eight others, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 榮乃開城門，延繼祖入，復捕斬二十六人。

translations.literal: Rong then opened the city gate, welcomed Jizu inside, and again captured and executed twenty-six men.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then opened the city gates, welcomed Jizu inside, and captured and executed twenty-six more men.

sentences.zh: 錄功，擢光祿寺少卿，再遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred again to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded, and he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then transferred again to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以右僉都御史巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Gansu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Gansu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 魯迷貢使留甘州者九十余人，總兵官楊信驅以禦寇，死者十之一。

translations.literal: More than ninety Rumi tribute envoys remaining at Ganzhou were driven by Commander-in-Chief Yang Xin to resist bandits, and one in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: More than ninety Rumi tribute envoys still at Ganzhou were driven by Commander-in-Chief Yang Xin to fight bandits, and one in ten of them died.

sentences.zh: 榮言：「彼以好來，而用之鋒鏑，失遠人心，且示中國弱。

translations.literal: Rong said, "They came in friendship, yet were put to the edge of sword and spear; this loses the hearts of distant peoples and moreover shows China to be weak."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "They came in friendship, yet were sent into battle; this alienates distant peoples and shows the Middle Kingdom to be weak."

sentences.zh: 」詔奪信官，槥死者送之歸。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Xin of his office, placed the dead in coffins, and sent them home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped Xin of his office, placed the dead in coffins, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 番人感悅。

translations.literal: The frontier peoples were moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以大同巡撫趙錦與總兵官周尚文不相能，詔榮與錦易任。

translations.literal: The following year, because Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin of Datong and Commander-in-Chief Zhou Shangwen could not get along, an edict ordered Rong and Jin to exchange posts.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because Grand Coordinator Zhao Jin of Datong and Commander-in-Chief Zhou Shangwen could not work together, an edict ordered Rong and Jin to exchange posts.

sentences.zh: 俺答數萬騎入掠，榮與尚文破之黑山陽，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: Altan Khan entered with tens of thousands of horsemen to raid; Rong and Shangwen defeated him south of Heishan, and Rong was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Altan Khan entered with tens of thousands of horsemen to raid; Rong and Shangwen defeated him south of Heishan, and Rong was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 寇復大舉犯中路，參將張鳳等陣歿。

translations.literal: The bandits again mounted a major assault on the central route, and Brigade Commander Zhang Feng and others fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits again mounted a major assault on the central route, and Brigade Commander Zhang Feng and others fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 榮與尚文及總督翁萬達嚴兵備陽和，而遣騎邀擊，多所殺傷，寇乃引去。

translations.literal: Rong, Shangwen, and Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda rigorously prepared defenses at Yanghe, while dispatching cavalry to intercept and attack, killing and wounding many; the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Rong, Shangwen, and Grand Coordinator Weng Wanda rigorously prepared defenses at Yanghe while dispatching cavalry to intercept the enemy, killing and wounding many; the bandits then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 代府奉國將軍充灼行剽，榮奏奪其祿。

translations.literal: Chongzhuo, a Fengguo General of the Prince of Dai's household, went about plundering; Rong memorialized to strip him of his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhuo, a Fengguo General of the Prince of Dai's household, went about plundering; Rong memorialized to strip him of his stipend.

sentences.zh: 充灼等結小王子入寇，謀據大同。

translations.literal: Chongzhuo and others joined with the Little Prince to invade and plotted to seize Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhuo and others joined with the Little Prince to invade and plotted to seize Datong.

sentences.zh: 榮告尚文捕得，皆伏辜。

translations.literal: Rong informed Shangwen, who captured them; all suffered punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rong informed Shangwen, who captured them; all were duly punished.

sentences.zh: 榮以大同無險，乃築東路邊牆百三十八里，堡七，墩台百五十四。

translations.literal: Because Rong considered Datong to have no natural defenses, he built one hundred thirty-eight li of border wall on the eastern route, seven forts, and one hundred fifty-four beacon towers.
translations.idiomatic: Because Rong considered Datong to lack natural defenses, he built one hundred thirty-eight li of border wall on the eastern route, along with seven forts and one hundred fifty-four beacon towers.

sentences.zh: 又以守邊當積粟。

translations.literal: He also held that defending the frontier required accumulating grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that defending the frontier required stockpiling grain.

sentences.zh: 而近邊弘賜諸堡三十一所，延亙五百餘里，辟治之皆膏腴田，可數十萬頃。

translations.literal: Moreover, the thirty-one forts such as Hongci along the near frontier stretched continuously for more than five hundred li; once cleared and developed, they were all fertile fields amounting to several hundred thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the thirty-one forts such as Hongci along the near frontier stretched continuously for more than five hundred li; once cleared and developed, they were all fertile land amounting to several hundred thousand qing.

sentences.zh: 乃奏請召軍佃作，復其租徭，移大同一歲市馬費市牛賦之；

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized requesting that troops be summoned to tenant-farm the land, restoring their rents and corvée exemptions, and that Datong's annual horse-purchase funds be redirected to buy oxen and distribute them;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized requesting that troops be summoned to farm the land as tenants, with their rents and corvée exemptions restored, and that Datong's annual horse-purchase funds be redirected to buy oxen and distribute them;

sentences.zh: 秋冬則聚而遏寇。

translations.literal: in autumn and winter they would gather to repel bandits.
translations.idiomatic: in autumn and winter they would gather to repel invaders.

sentences.zh: 帝立從焉。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 寇入犯，與尚文破之彌陀山，斬一部長。

translations.literal: When bandits entered to raid, he and Shangwen defeated them at Mount Mile and beheaded one tribal chief.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits invaded, he and Shangwen defeated them at Mount Mile and beheaded one tribal chief.

sentences.zh: 榮先以靖亂功，進兵部右侍郎，又以繕邊破敵，累被獎賚。

translations.literal: Rong had first been promoted to Vice Minister of War on account of his merit in quelling the mutiny, and was repeatedly rewarded for repairing the frontier and defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had first been promoted to Vice Minister of War for quelling the mutiny, and was repeatedly rewarded for fortifying the frontier and defeating the enemy.

sentences.zh: 召還理部事，進左。

translations.literal: He was recalled to manage the ministry's affairs and promoted to the left vice ministership.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to manage the ministry's affairs and promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙廷瑞罷，榮署部務，奏行秋防十事。

translations.literal: When Minister Zhao Tingrui was dismissed, Rong acted in the ministry's affairs and memorialized ten autumn defense measures for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Zhao Tingrui was dismissed, Rong acted in the minister's stead and memorialized ten autumn defense measures for implementation.

sentences.zh: 已而翁萬達入為尚書，遭母喪，榮復當署部務，辭疾乞休。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Weng Wanda entered the capital as minister; when he suffered his mother's death, Rong again was to act in the ministry's affairs, but he pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Weng Wanda entered the capital as minister; when he entered mourning for his mother, Rong was again expected to act in the minister's stead, but he pleaded illness and requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪職閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, stripped him of office, and ordered him to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, stripped him of office, and ordered him to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 越二年卒。

translations.literal: Two years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died.

sentences.zh: 當榮之撫大同也，萬達為總督，尚文為總兵。

translations.literal: When Rong was grand coordinator of Datong, Weng Wanda was supreme commander and Shangwen was commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong served as grand coordinator of Datong, Weng Wanda was supreme commander and Zhou Shangwen was commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 三人皆有才略，寇數入不能得志。

translations.literal: All three possessed talent and strategy; though bandits entered repeatedly, they could not achieve their aims.
translations.idiomatic: All three were men of talent and strategy; though bandits raided repeatedly, they could not achieve their aims.

sentences.zh: 自後代者不能任，寇無歲不入躪邊，人益思榮等。

translations.literal: Afterward their successors could not fill the role; bandits invaded and trampled the frontier every year, and people increasingly longed for Rong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward their successors could not fill their shoes; bandits invaded the frontier every year, and people increasingly longed for Rong and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 明年，俺答薄京師，萬達、榮皆已去。

translations.literal: The next year Altan Khan approached the capital; Wanda and Rong had both already departed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Altan Khan approached the capital; Weng Wanda and Zhan Rong had both already left office.

sentences.zh: 論者謂二人在，寇未必至此。

translations.literal: Commentators said that had the two men still been in office, the bandits might not have reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that had the two men still been in office, the bandits might never have come so close.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，榮孫延為順天通判，上書訟榮功。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, Rong's grandson Yan, serving as assistant prefect of Shuntian, submitted a memorial pleading Rong's merits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, Rong's grandson Yan, serving as assistant prefect of Shuntian, submitted a memorial pleading Rong's merits.

sentences.zh: 贈工部尚書，予恤如制。

translations.literal: Rong was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and mourning stipends were given according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Works, and mourning stipends were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 劉源清，字汝澄，東平人。

translations.literal: Liu Yuanqing, styled Rucheng, was a native of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuanqing, styled Rucheng, was a native of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 正德九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of the Zhengde reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 授進賢知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，源清積薪環室，命家人曰：「事急，火吾家。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled, Yuanqing piled firewood around his rooms and ordered his household, "If matters grow urgent, burn our house."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Ning Chen Hao rebelled, Yuanqing piled firewood around his rooms and told his household, "If matters grow urgent, burn our house."

sentences.zh: 」一僕逸，手刃以徇。

translations.literal: One servant escaped; he killed him with his own hand as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: One servant escaped; he killed him with his own hand as a warning to the rest.

sentences.zh: 縣中諸惡少與賊通者，悉杖殺之。

translations.literal: All the delinquent youths in the county who communicated with the rebels he beat to death.
translations.idiomatic: He beat to death every delinquent youth in the county who had communicated with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 宸濠妃弟婁伯歸上饒募兵，源清邀戮之。

translations.literal: Lou Bo, younger brother of Chen Hao's consort, returned to Shangrao to raise troops; Yuanqing intercepted and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Bo, younger brother of Chen Hao's consort, returned to Shangrao to raise troops; Yuanqing intercepted and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊檄至，立斬其使。

translations.literal: When a rebel proclamation arrived, he immediately beheaded its bearer.
translations.idiomatic: When a rebel proclamation arrived, he immediately beheaded its bearer.

sentences.zh: 會余幹知縣馬津、龍津驛丞孫天祐亦起兵拒賊。

translations.literal: At the same time Magistrate Ma Jin of Yugan and Sun Tianyou, assistant at Longjin Post, also raised troops to resist the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Magistrate Ma Jin of Yugan and Sun Tianyou, assistant at Longjin Post, also raised troops to resist the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊七殿下者，奪運舟于龍津，天祐與戰，殺數人。

translations.literal: A rebel known as the Seventh Prince's son seized transport boats at Longjin; Tianyou fought him and killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel known as the Seventh Prince's son seized transport boats at Longjin; Tianyou fought him and killed several men.

sentences.zh: 賊党募兵過龍津，天祐追殺之，焚其舟。

translations.literal: Rebel partisans raising troops passed through Longjin; Tianyou pursued and killed them and burned their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel partisans raising troops passed through Longjin; Tianyou pursued them, killed them, and burned their boats.

sentences.zh: 婁氏家眾西下，亦為天祐所遏，擒七十餘人。

translations.literal: The Lou clan's household followers moving west were also blocked by Tianyou, who captured more than seventy men.
translations.idiomatic: The Lou clan's household followers moving west were also blocked by Tianyou, who captured more than seventy men.

sentences.zh: 賊兵不敢經湖東以窺兩浙者，三人力也。

translations.literal: That rebel troops did not dare pass east of the lake to spy on the two Zhe provinces was due to the efforts of these three men.
translations.idiomatic: That rebel troops did not dare pass east of the lake to threaten the two Zhe provinces was due to the efforts of these three men.

sentences.zh: 賊平，源清征為御史。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was suppressed, Yuanqing was summoned to serve as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was suppressed, Yuanqing was summoned to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，津亦入為御史。

translations.literal: When the Jiajing reign began, Jin also entered the capital as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign began, Ma Jin also entered the capital as a censor.

sentences.zh: 津，滁州人。

translations.literal: Jin was a native of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jin was a native of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 終福建副使。

translations.literal: He ended his career as vice commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 源清尋遷大理丞，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Yuanqing soon transferred to be a vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing soon transferred to serve as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then returned home citing illness.

sentences.zh: 六年夏，以右僉都御史巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the summer of the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the sixth year, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu with the rank of Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 滴水崖賊郭春據城叛，稱王。

translations.literal: The bandit Guo Chun of Dishui Cliff seized the city in rebellion and declared himself king.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Guo Chun of Dishui Cliff seized the city in rebellion and declared himself king.

sentences.zh: 源清遣卒捕之，為所覺。

translations.literal: Yuanqing dispatched soldiers to capture him, but they were discovered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing dispatched soldiers to capture him, but they were discovered.

sentences.zh: 副總兵劉淵令曰「止擒元惡」，以旗繞城而呼。

translations.literal: Vice Commander Liu Yuan issued the order "Only capture the chief culprit," and with banners circled the city shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commander Liu Yuan issued the order "Only capture the chief culprit" and, with banners unfurled, circled the city shouting the proclamation.

sentences.zh: 其黨皆散，春等自剄死。

translations.literal: His followers all dispersed; Chun and the others cut their own throats and died.
translations.idiomatic: His followers all dispersed; Chun and the others cut their own throats and died.

sentences.zh: 總兵官郤永虐下，源清劾罷之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong abused his subordinates; Yuanqing impeached him and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong abused his subordinates; Yuanqing impeached him and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 進副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以邊警遷兵部左侍郎，總制宣、大、山西、保定諸鎮軍務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, on account of frontier alarms he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs in the garrisons of Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, on account of frontier alarms he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs in the garrisons of Xuanfu, Datong, Shanxi, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 大同總兵官李瑾浚天城左孤店濠四十里，趣工急。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Li Jin of Datong excavated a forty-li moat at the left solitary post of Tiancheng, pressing the work urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Li Jin of Datong excavated a forty-li moat at the left solitary post of Tiancheng, pressing the labor urgently.

sentences.zh: 卒王福勝等焚殺瑾，因焚巡撫潘亻放署。

translations.literal: The soldiers Wang Fusheng and others burned and killed Jin, and also burned the yamen of Grand Coordinator Pan Fang.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers Wang Fusheng and others burned and killed Jin, and also burned the yamen of Grand Coordinator Pan Fang.

sentences.zh: 亻放奏瑾激變，帝命源清同總兵郤永討之。

translations.literal: Pan Fang memorialized that Jin had provoked the mutiny; the emperor ordered Yuanqing together with Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fang memorialized that Jin had provoked the mutiny; the emperor ordered Yuanqing together with Commander-in-Chief Xi Yong to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 源清榜令解散。

translations.literal: Yuanqing posted a proclamation ordering dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing posted a proclamation ordering the mutineers to disperse.

sentences.zh: 而榜言五堡變，處之過寬，五堡遺孽大懼。

translations.literal: But the proclamation spoke of the Five Forts mutiny and said it had been treated too leniently; the surviving remnants of the Five Forts were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: But the proclamation spoke of the Five Forts mutiny and said it had been treated too leniently; the surviving remnants of the Five Forts were terrified.

sentences.zh: 師次陽和，亻放等密捕亂卒杖死十餘人，系賊首王保等七十餘人以獻，請旋師。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Yanghe, Pan Fang and others secretly captured mutinous soldiers and beat more than ten to death, bound the rebel leaders Wang Bao and more than seventy others and presented them, and requested withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the army halted at Yanghe, Pan Fang and others secretly captured mutinous soldiers and beat more than ten to death, bound the rebel leaders Wang Bao and more than seventy others and presented them, and requested that the army withdraw.

sentences.zh: 源清懲昔胡瓚事，不欲已，以囚屬御史蘇祐。

translations.literal: Yuanqing, chastened by the earlier affair of Hu Zan, did not wish to stop; he entrusted the prisoners to Censor Su You.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing, chastened by the earlier affair of Hu Zan, did not wish to stop; he entrusted the prisoners to Censor Su You.

sentences.zh: 囚妄言前總兵硃振失職首亂，且多引無辜。

translations.literal: The prisoners falsely claimed that the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen had failed in duty and started the mutiny, and moreover implicated many innocent men.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoners falsely claimed that the former commander-in-chief Zhu Zhen had failed in duty and started the mutiny, and implicated many innocent men besides.

sentences.zh: 源清遣參將趙綱入城大索。

translations.literal: Yuanqing dispatched Brigade Commander Zhao Gang to enter the city and conduct a thorough search.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing dispatched Brigade Commander Zhao Gang to enter the city and conduct a thorough search.

sentences.zh: 城中訛言城且屠，亂卒遂鼓噪，殺千戶張欽。

translations.literal: A false rumor spread in the city that it was about to be massacred; the mutinous soldiers then clamored in uproar and killed Thousand-Household Commander Zhang Qin.
translations.idiomatic: A false rumor spread through the city that a massacre was imminent; the mutinous soldiers then erupted in uproar and killed Thousand-Household Commander Zhang Qin.

sentences.zh: 會僉事孫允中自源清所至，諭源清意，撫慰之始定。

translations.literal: As it happened Vice Commissioner Sun Yunzhong came from Yuanqing's camp, explained Yuanqing's intent, and only after pacifying them did calm return.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened Vice Commissioner Sun Yunzhong came from Yuanqing's camp, explained Yuanqing's intent, and only after pacifying them did the city settle down.

sentences.zh: 振前為亂卒所擁，實不反，詣源清自明。

translations.literal: Zhen had earlier been coerced by the mutinous soldiers and in fact had not rebelled; he went to Yuanqing to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had earlier been coerced by the mutinous soldiers and had not in fact rebelled; he went to Yuanqing to clear himself.

sentences.zh: 不能白，發憤自殺。

translations.literal: He could not clear himself, and in indignation killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to clear his name, he killed himself in a fit of rage.

sentences.zh: 永兵至城下大掠，五堡遺孽遂盡反。

translations.literal: Yong's troops reached the foot of the city and plundered on a great scale; the surviving remnants of the Five Forts then all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong's troops reached the city and looted it heavily, the surviving mutineers from the Five Forts rose in full revolt.

sentences.zh: 迎戰，殺遊擊曹安。

translations.literal: They met the attack in battle and killed Mobile Corps Commander Cao An.
translations.idiomatic: They gave battle and killed Mobile Corps Commander Cao An.

sentences.zh: 官軍攻據四關，晝夜圍擊。

translations.literal: The government troops attacked and seized the four passes, besieging and striking day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops seized the four passes and pressed the siege day and night.

sentences.zh: 亂卒出前參將黃鎮等於獄，奉為帥，死守。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers released the former brigade commander Huang Zhen and others from prison, made them commanders, and held out to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers freed the former brigade commander Huang Zhen and others from prison, proclaimed them leaders, and resolved to hold the city at all costs.

sentences.zh: 亻放與鎮國將軍俊郐隱等登城，止毋攻。

translations.literal: Pan Fang together with State Stabilizing General Jun Guiyin and others mounted the wall and ordered that there be no attack.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fang, State Stabilizing General Jun Guiyin, and others climbed the wall and called for a halt to the assault.

sentences.zh: 俊郐隱出見永請緩兵，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Jun Guiyin went out to see Yong and begged that the troops be eased; none would listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Guiyin went out to meet Yong and pleaded for a reprieve from military pressure, but his appeals went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 允中縋城出，言將士妄殺狀。

translations.literal: Yunzhong was lowered by rope from the wall and reported the condition of the troops' indiscriminate killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong was lowered by rope from the wall to report how the soldiers had been killing without cause.

sentences.zh: 源清叱曰：「汝為賊遊說耶！

translations.literal: Yuanqing shouted at him, "Are you pleading the rebels' case!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing rebuked him: "Are you acting as an advocate for the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」欲囚之。

translations.literal: He wished to imprison him.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to have him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 允中不敢歸。

translations.literal: Yunzhong did not dare return.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzhong did not dare go back into the city.

sentences.zh: 源清因多設邏卒，遏王府及有司軍民章疏，而請益師至五萬。

translations.literal: Yuanqing therefore set up many patrol guards, blocked memorials from the princely establishment and from officials, soldiers, and civilians, and requested reinforcements of up to fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing posted additional patrol guards, cut off memorials from the princely establishment and from officials, soldiers, and civilians alike, and asked that reinforcements be raised to fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝命侍郎錢如京、都督江桓統京軍八千以往。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Qian Rujing and Regional Commander Jiang Huan to lead eight thousand capital troops thither.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Qian Rujing and Regional Commander Jiang Huan to lead eight thousand capital troops to the scene.

sentences.zh: 已忽悟，罷弗遣，專責源清、永討賊。

translations.literal: Then he suddenly understood, canceled the dispatch, and charged Yuanqing and Yong alone with suppressing the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He soon thought better of it, canceled the dispatch, and held Yuanqing and Yong solely responsible for suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 亻放馳疏言，將士妄殺激變，速旋師，亂中已。

translations.literal: Pan Fang sent an urgent memorial saying that the troops' indiscriminate killing had provoked the mutiny, that the army should be withdrawn at once, and that the disorder among them was already settled.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fang sent an urgent memorial arguing that the soldiers' reckless killings had provoked the revolt, urging an immediate withdrawal of the army, and declaring that the turmoil among the mutineers had already subsided.

sentences.zh: 源清亦詆亻放媚賊。

translations.literal: Yuanqing also denounced Pan Fang for currying favor with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing in turn accused Pan Fang of appeasing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 張孚敬主源清，侍郎顧鼎臣、黃綰言用兵謬，帝不能決。

translations.literal: Zhang Fuyi sided with Yuanqing; Vice Ministers Gu Dingchen and Huang Wan said that resorting to arms was mistaken; the emperor could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuyi backed Yuanqing, while Vice Ministers Gu Dingchen and Huang Wan argued that military action was misguided, and the emperor could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 城圍久大困，毀王府及諸廨舍供爨。

translations.literal: The siege dragged on and the city was greatly distressed; they destroyed the princely residence and the various offices to supply fuel for cooking.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege wore on, the city fell into desperate straits; the rebels tore down the princely residence and government offices for firewood.

sentences.zh: 兵部復下安撫令，源清亦樹幟招降，叛卒稍稍自投。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War again issued orders of pacification; Yuanqing also raised banners to summon surrender, and the rebel soldiers gradually came forward of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War issued another pacification order; Yuanqing also raised banners offering surrender, and rebel soldiers began to give themselves up one after another.

sentences.zh: 首惡黃鎮等亦分日出見，乞通樵采路，永許諾。

translations.literal: The chief culprits Huang Zhen and others also came out on successive days and begged that a path for gathering firewood be opened; Yong promised it.
translations.idiomatic: The ringleaders Huang Zhen and others also came out on successive days, asking that a route be opened for gathering firewood; Yong agreed.

sentences.zh: 翌日采薪者出，永悉執之。

translations.literal: The next day those who went out to gather firewood emerged, and Yong seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when wood-gatherers came out, Yong had them all arrested.

sentences.zh: 城中人益懼，亂卒復叛，勾外寇為助。

translations.literal: The people in the city grew still more afraid; the mutinous soldiers rebelled again and summoned outside raiders as allies.
translations.idiomatic: Terror spread through the city; the mutineers rebelled again and called in outside raiders for support.

sentences.zh: 永遇之，大敗而遁。

translations.literal: Yong encountered them, was utterly defeated, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yong met them in battle, suffered a crushing defeat, and fled.

sentences.zh: 叛卒遂引寇十餘騎入城，指代府曰：「以此為那顏居。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers then led more than ten mounted raiders into the city, pointed at the Princely Establishment of Dai, and said, "Let this be the nayan's dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then ushered more than a dozen mounted raiders into the city, pointed at the Princely Establishment of Dai, and said, "This shall be the nayan's residence."

sentences.zh: 」「那顏」者，華言大人也。

translations.literal: "Nayan" is the Chinese word for "great man."
translations.idiomatic: "Nayan" means "great lord" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 城中人聞之，皆巷哭。

translations.literal: When the people in the city heard this, all wept in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: When the townspeople heard this, wailing broke out in every lane.

sentences.zh: 明日，外寇攻東南二關，叛卒與犄角，官軍殊死戰，互有殺傷。

translations.literal: The next day the outside raiders attacked the two southeastern passes; the rebel soldiers coordinated with them in pincer fashion; the government troops fought to the death, and each side inflicted casualties.
translations.idiomatic: The next day outside raiders assaulted the two southeastern passes while the rebels coordinated in pincer fashion; government troops fought desperately, and both sides suffered killed and wounded.

sentences.zh: 寇知叛卒不足賴，倒戈擊之，大詬而去。

translations.literal: The raiders knew the rebel soldiers could not be relied upon, turned their blades against them, cursed them bitterly, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the rebels unreliable, the raiders turned on them, hurled abuse, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是時，寇游騎南掠至朔、應。

translations.literal: At this time the raiders' roaming cavalry plundered south as far as Shuo and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile, raiding cavalry swept south as far as Shuo and Ying.

sentences.zh: 源清請募九邊兵，增總制官禦之，己得一意攻城，帝不許。

translations.literal: Yuanqing requested that troops be recruited from the Nine Garrisons and that an additional overall commander be appointed to repel them, so that he himself might concentrate solely on attacking the city; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing asked to raise troops from the Nine Garrisons and appoint an additional overall commander to hold them off, so that he could devote himself entirely to the siege; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 源清乃百道攻，穴城，為毒煙熏死者相籍。

translations.literal: Yuanqing then attacked by a hundred routes, tunneled under the wall, and those who died from poisonous smoke lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing then assaulted the city from every direction, tunneled beneath the walls, and the dead from poisonous smoke lay heaped together.

sentences.zh: 復請壅水灌之。

translations.literal: He again requested that water be dammed up to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed damming the water to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 帝大不懌，奪其職閑住，以兵部侍郎張瓚代之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly displeased, stripped him of his post and ordered him to live in retirement, and replaced him with Vice Minister of War Zhang Zan.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly displeased, the emperor stripped him of office and ordered him to live in retirement, replacing him with Vice Minister of War Zhang Zan.

sentences.zh: 瓚未至，郎中詹榮等已悉捕首惡。

translations.literal: Before Zan arrived, Director Zhan Rong and others had already captured all the chief culprits.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhang Zan even arrived, Director Zhan Rong and others had already captured all the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 黃綰勘功罪，言源清、永實罪魁，具劾其婪賄不貲狀。

translations.literal: Huang Wan assessed merit and guilt, saying that Yuanqing and Yong were in fact the chief culprits, and fully impeached them for their greedy acceptance of bribes beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Wan reviewed the record of merit and blame, declaring Yuanqing and Yong the true instigators, and impeached them in detail for extortionate bribery.

sentences.zh: 兵科曾忭等言，宸濠亂，源清有保障功，當蒙八議之貸。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zeng Bian and others said that during the Chen Hao rebellion Yuanqing had rendered meritorious service in defense and ought to receive the leniency of the Eight Deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zeng Bian and others argued that during Prince Ning's rebellion Yuanqing had distinguished himself in defense and deserved the leniency granted under the Eight Deliberations.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下忭等詔獄，逮源清治之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, sent Bian and the others to the imperial prison, and had Yuanqing arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor sent Bian and the others to the imperial prison and had Yuanqing arrested for trial.

sentences.zh: 獄久不決，綰憂去，乃減死，斥為民。

translations.literal: The case long went unresolved; Wan left office in distress; finally the sentence was reduced from death, and Yuanqing was banished to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: The case dragged on without resolution; Wan left office in distress; in the end the death sentence was commuted and Yuanqing was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 俺答薄京師，即家起之，未赴而卒。

translations.literal: When Altan approached the capital, Yuanqing was summoned from his home to office, but before he could take up the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan threatened the capital, Yuanqing was recalled from retirement, but he died before he could report for duty.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, he was posthumously granted the title Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Longqing reign, he was posthumously honored as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 劉天和，字養和，麻城人。

translations.literal: Liu Tianhe, styled Yanghe, was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianhe, styled Yanghe, was a native of Macheng.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a presented scholar in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Zhengde 3.

sentences.zh: 授南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾黜御史十八人，改他曹二十四人補之，天和與焉。

translations.literal: Liu Jin dismissed eighteen censors and transferred twenty-four men from other offices to fill the posts; Tianhe was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin dismissed eighteen censors and filled the vacancies with twenty-four men transferred from other offices, Tianhe was among those appointed.

sentences.zh: 出按陝西。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官廖堂奉詔辦食禦物於蘭州，天和謂非所部，辭不往。

translations.literal: The eunuch commissioner Liao Tang received an edict to procure imperial provisions at Lanzhou; Tianhe said it was not within his jurisdiction and declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuch commissioner Liao Tang was ordered by imperial edict to procure imperial provisions at Lanzhou, Tianhe held that the matter lay outside his jurisdiction and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 堂奏天和拒命，詔逮之。

translations.literal: Tang memorialized that Tianhe had defied orders; an edict was issued to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang memorialized that Tianhe had defied orders, and an edict was issued for his arrest.

sentences.zh: 部民哭送者萬人。

translations.literal: Ten thousand people of the province wept as they saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand people of the province wept as they escorted him away.

sentences.zh: 錮詔獄久不釋，吏部尚書楊一清疏救，法司奏當贖杖還職，中旨謫金壇丞。

translations.literal: He was confined in the imperial prison for a long time without release; Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing memorialized in his defense; the judicial offices reported that he should be ransomed with a beating and restored to office; but by secret edict he was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Held long in the imperial prison, he was defended in a memorial by Minister of Personnel Yang Yiqing; the judicial offices recommended ransom by beating and restoration to office, but a secret edict instead demoted him to assistant magistrate of Jintan.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事孫繼芳抗章救，不報。

translations.literal: Secretary Sun Jifang of the Ministry of Punishments submitted a forceful memorial in his defense; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jifang, a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, submitted an impassioned memorial in his defense, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 屢遷湖州知府，多惠政。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he became prefect of Huzhou, where he enacted many benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became prefect of Huzhou, where he carried out many policies that benefited the people.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，擢山西提學副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Education in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jiajing reign he was promoted to Vice Commissioner for Education in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京太常少卿。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he became Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以右僉都御史督甘肅屯政。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he supervised agricultural colonization in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise agricultural colonization in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 請以肅州丁壯及山、陝流民于近邊耕牧，且推行于諸邊。

translations.literal: He requested that able-bodied men of Suzhou and displaced persons from Shanxi and Shaanxi be settled to farm and herd on the near frontier, and that the policy be extended to the various border regions.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed settling able-bodied men from Suzhou and displaced people from Shanxi and Shaanxi to farm and herd along the near frontier, and extending the policy to other border regions.

sentences.zh: 尋奏當興革者十事，田利大興。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized ten measures that should be instituted or abolished, and agricultural profit greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted a memorial outlining ten reforms to institute or abolish, and agricultural productivity rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 改撫陝西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 請撤鎮守中官及罷為民患者三十余事，帝皆從之。

translations.literal: He requested the removal of eunuch commissioners and the abolition of more than thirty practices harmful to the people; the emperor approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for the removal of eunuch commissioners and the abolition of more than thirty practices that harmed the people; the emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 洮、岷番四十二族蠢動，天和誅不順命者。

translations.literal: The forty-two Tibetan tribes of Tao and Min stirred restlessly; Tianhe executed those who disobeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: When the forty-two Tibetan tribes of Tao and Min grew restless, Tianhe executed those who defied his authority.

sentences.zh: 又討平湖店大盜及漢中妖賊，就進右副都御史。

translations.literal: He also suppressed the great bandits of Pinghu Store and the sorcerer-rebels of Hanzhong, and on the spot was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He also suppressed the major bandits of Pinghu Store and the sorcerer-rebels of Hanzhong, and was promoted on the spot to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋以故官總理河道。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed in his former rank to take overall charge of the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: After observing mourning for his mother, he returned to his former rank to take overall charge of the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 黃河南徙，曆濟、徐皆旁溢。

translations.literal: The Yellow River shifted eastward, and through Ji and Xu it overflowed on every side.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River shifted eastward, flooding the regions of Ji and Xu on every side.

sentences.zh: 天和疏汴河，自硃仙鎮至沛飛雲橋，殺其下流。

translations.literal: Tianhe dredged the Bian River from Zhuxian Town to Feiyun Bridge in Pei, reducing its lower course.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe dredged the Bian River from Zhuxian Town to Feiyun Bridge in Pei, cutting back its lower channel.

sentences.zh: 疏山東七十二泉，自鳧、尼諸山達南旺河，浚其下流。

translations.literal: He dredged the seventy-two springs of Shandong from Mount Fu, Mount Ni, and the other mountains to the Nanwang River, clearing their lower courses.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the seventy-two springs of Shandong from Mount Fu, Mount Ni, and neighboring peaks down to the Nanwang River, dredging their lower channels.

sentences.zh: 役夫二萬，不三月訖工。

translations.literal: Twenty thousand laborers were employed, and within three months the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: With twenty thousand laborers, the work was completed in less than three months.

sentences.zh: 加工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Right Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 故事，河南八府歲役民治河，不赴役者人出銀三兩。

translations.literal: By precedent the eight prefectures of Henan annually conscripted the people for river work; those who did not report for corvée paid three taels of silver each.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the eight prefectures of Henan conscripted the populace each year for river work; those who failed to report for corvée paid three taels of silver apiece.

sentences.zh: 天和因歲饑，請盡蠲旁河受役者課，遠河未役者半之。

translations.literal: Because of famine that year, Tianhe requested that the levies on those conscripted along the river be wholly remitted, and that those farther from the river who had not yet served pay half.
translations.idiomatic: Citing the year's famine, Tianhe asked that levies on those conscripted along the river be fully remitted and that those farther from the river who had not yet served pay only half.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved by edict.

sentences.zh: 十五年改兵部左侍郎，總制三邊軍務。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs on the Three Frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs on the Three Frontiers.

sentences.zh: 兵車皆雙輪，用二十人，遇險即困，又行遲不適於用。

translations.literal: The military wagons all had double wheels and required twenty men; they became stuck whenever the terrain grew difficult, and they were also slow and unsuited to use.
translations.idiomatic: Military wagons all had double wheels and required twenty men to move; they bogged down on difficult terrain and were too slow to be of practical use.

sentences.zh: 天和請仿前總督秦紘只輪車，上置砲槍斧戟，廂前樹狻猊牌，左右虎盾，連二車可蔽三四十人。

translations.literal: Tianhe requested that they follow the former overall commander Qin Hong's single-wheeled cart, mounting cannon, muskets, axes, and halberds upon it, setting suanni shields before the carriage box and tiger shields to left and right; two carts linked together could shelter thirty or forty men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe proposed reviving the single-wheeled cart used by the former overall commander Qin Hong, fitted with cannon, muskets, axes, and halberds, with suanni shields mounted before the carriage box and tiger shields to either side; two carts linked together could shelter thirty or forty men.

sentences.zh: 一人挽之，推且翼者各二人。

translations.literal: One man pulled it, and two men each pushed and flanked it.
translations.idiomatic: One man hauled it while two pushed and two flanked it on either side.

sentences.zh: 戰則護騎士其中，敵遠則施火器，稍近發弓弩，又近乃出短兵，敵走則騎兵追。

translations.literal: In battle cavalry were protected within; when the enemy was distant they employed firearms; at closer range they shot bows and crossbows; at still closer range they drew short weapons; when the enemy fled cavalry pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In battle cavalry sheltered inside; at long range they used firearms, at medium range bows and crossbows, and at close quarters short weapons; when the enemy fled, cavalry gave chase.

sentences.zh: 復製隨車小帳，令士不露宿。

translations.literal: He also devised small tents to accompany the carts, so that the soldiers need not sleep in the open.
translations.idiomatic: He also designed small tents to accompany the carts so that soldiers would not have to sleep in the open.

sentences.zh: 又毒弩矢，修邊牆濠塹。

translations.literal: He also poisoned crossbow bolts and repaired the border wall and moats.
translations.idiomatic: He also had crossbow bolts poisoned and had the border wall and moats repaired.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All of these proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 吉囊十萬眾屯賀蘭山後，遣別部寇涼州，副將王輔逐奪其纛。

translations.literal: Jinjang encamped with a hundred thousand men behind Helan Mountain and sent a separate force to raid Liangzhou; Vice General Wang Fu pursued and seized their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Jinjang encamped with a hundred thousand men behind Helan Mountain and sent a detached force to raid Liangzhou; Vice General Wang Fu pursued them and captured their battle standard.

sentences.zh: 寇莊浪，總兵官姜奭屢敗之。

translations.literal: The raiders entered Zhuanglang; Commander-in-Chief Jiang Shi repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders entered Zhuanglang, Commander-in-Chief Jiang Shi defeated them repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 進天和右都御史。

translations.literal: Tianhe was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 寇復大集兵將入犯。

translations.literal: The raiders again gathered their forces in strength and were about to invade.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders again mustered a large force and prepared to invade.

sentences.zh: 天和策寇瞰西有備必東，密檄延綏副將白爵宵行，與參將吳瑛合。

translations.literal: Tianhe calculated that seeing preparations in the west the raiders would surely strike east, and secretly dispatched a sealed order to Yan-sui Vice General Bai Jue to march by night and join Brigade Commander Wu Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe reasoned that seeing defenses massed in the west, the raiders would surely strike east; he secretly ordered Yan-sui Vice General Bai Jue to march by night and join Brigade Commander Wu Ying.

sentences.zh: 寇果東入黑河墩，遇爵伏兵，大創而去。

translations.literal: The raiders indeed entered east at Heihe Dun, encountered Jue's ambush, suffered a heavy blow, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did strike east at Heihe Dun, ran into Jue's ambush, suffered heavy losses, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 既又入蒺藜川，爵尾擊之，寇多死。

translations.literal: Later they entered again at Jili Chuan; Jue struck them from the rear, and many raiders died.
translations.idiomatic: They later entered Jili Chuan again; Jue struck from the rear and killed many of them.

sentences.zh: 尋入寇家澗、張家塔，為爵、瑛所敗。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they raided Jiajian and Zhangjiata; they were defeated by Jue and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: They soon raided Jiajian and Zhangjiata and were defeated by Jue and Ying.

sentences.zh: 犯寧夏者，總兵官王效復破之。

translations.literal: Those who invaded Ningxia were again defeated by Commander-in-Chief Wang Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Those who struck at Ningxia were in turn defeated by Commander-in-Chief Wang Xiao.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，進天和左都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and promoted Tianhe to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly pleased, the emperor promoted Tianhe to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 吉囊犯河西，天和禦卻之，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Jinjang invaded Hexi; Tianhe repelled him and was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinjang invaded Hexi, Tianhe drove him back and was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 寇將入平虜城，天和伏兵花馬池。

translations.literal: As the raiders were about to enter Pinglu City, Tianhe set an ambush at Huama Chi.
translations.idiomatic: As the raiders were about to enter Pinglu City, Tianhe laid an ambush at Huama Chi.

sentences.zh: 寇戰不勝，走河上。

translations.literal: The raiders fought without victory and fled toward the river.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to win the battle, the raiders fled toward the river.

sentences.zh: 遇伏兵，多死于水。

translations.literal: They encountered the ambush, and many died in the water.
translations.idiomatic: They ran into the ambush, and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 吉囊乘虛寇固原，剽掠且饜。

translations.literal: Jinjang seized the opportunity to raid Guyuan, plundering until sated.
translations.idiomatic: Jinjang seized the opening to raid Guyuan and looted his fill.

sentences.zh: 會淫潦，弓矢盡膠，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Just then heavy rains fell; bows and arrows were all glued up, and there was no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Just then torrential rains fell; bows and arrows were rendered useless by the damp, and morale collapsed.

sentences.zh: 而諸將多畏縮，天和斬指揮二人，召故總兵周尚文令立功。

translations.literal: Meanwhile many of the generals shrank in fear; Tianhe executed two commanders and summoned the former commander-in-chief Zhou Shangwen, ordering him to earn merit.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the generals hung back in fear; Tianhe executed two commanders and recalled the former commander-in-chief Zhou Shangwen, ordering him to redeem himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 會陝西總兵官魏時角寇至黑水苑，尚文盡銳夾擊，殺吉囊子小十王。

translations.literal: Just then, as Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief Wei Shi encountered the raiders at Heishui Garden, Shangwen threw all his elite forces into a pincer attack and killed Jinjang's son Xiaoshi Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the raiders reached Heishui Garden, Shaanxi Commander-in-Chief Wei Shi and Shangwen threw all their elite forces into a pincer attack and killed Jinjang's son Xiaoshi Wang.

sentences.zh: 寇退寧夏，巡撫楊守禮、總兵官任傑等復邀擊，敗之鐵柱泉，斬獲共四百四十餘級。

translations.literal: The raiders retreated toward Ningxia; Grand Coordinator Yang Shouli, Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie, and others again intercepted them, defeated them at Tiezhu Spring, and together beheaded and captured more than four hundred and forty.
translations.idiomatic: As the raiders fell back toward Ningxia, Grand Coordinator Yang Shouli, Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie, and others intercepted them again, defeating them at Tiezhu Spring with more than four hundred and forty heads taken and captives seized.

sentences.zh: 論功，加天和太子太保，廕一子錦衣千戶，前後齎銀幣十數。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed, Tianhe was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, one son was granted the hereditary post of commander of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and on more than ten occasions he was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When honors were distributed, Tianhe was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, one son was granted a hereditary post in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and he received silver and silks on more than ten occasions.

sentences.zh: 遷南京戶部尚書，召為兵部尚書督團營。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, then summoned to serve as Minister of War and supervise the Tuan battalions.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, then recalled to serve as Minister of War and supervise the Tuan battalions.

sentences.zh: 言官論天和衰老，遂乞休歸。

translations.literal: Censorial officials argued that Tianhe was aged, and he thereupon requested retirement and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial officials argued that Tianhe had grown too old for office, he requested retirement and returned home.

sentences.zh: 家居三年卒。

translations.literal: After three years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after returning home, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，諡莊襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian, with the posthumous title Zhuangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Zhuangxiang.

sentences.zh: 天和初舉進士，劉瑾欲與敘宗姓，謝不往。

translations.literal: When Tianhe first passed the jinshi examination, Liu Jin wished to establish a clan relationship with him; he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianhe first passed the metropolitan examination, Liu Jin wanted to claim a kinship with him through their shared surname; Tianhe declined and refused the overture.

sentences.zh: 晚年內召，陶仲文以刺迎，稱戚屬。

translations.literal: In his later years he was summoned to court; Tao Zhongwen greeted him with a calling card, claiming kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he was recalled to the capital; Tao Zhongwen came to meet him with a calling card claiming they were relatives.

sentences.zh: 天和返其刺曰：「誤矣，吾中外姻連無是人。

translations.literal: Tianhe returned the card, saying: "This is a mistake—among my kin by marriage within and beyond the court there is no such person.
translations.idiomatic: Tianhe returned the card with the words: "This is a mistake. Among my in-laws inside and outside the court, there is no such person.

sentences.zh: 」仲文恚，其罷官有力焉。

translations.literal: " Zhongwen was furious; he had no small part in Tianhe's dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Tao Zhongwen was furious and played a significant role in having him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 楊守禮，字秉節，蒲州人。

translations.literal: Yang Shouli, styled Bingjie, was a man of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouli, styled Bingjie, was a native of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the sixth year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 除戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，屢遷湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiajing reign he was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 以計擒公安賊魁。

translations.literal: By stratagem he captured the bandit chief of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He devised a stratagem that captured the bandit chieftain of Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 坐事謫敘州通判。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to vice prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to vice prefect of Xuzhou on account of an offense.

sentences.zh: 累遷右副都御史，巡撫四川。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 與副將何卿平諸番亂，齎銀幣。

translations.literal: Together with Vice General He Qing he pacified the various fan rebellions and was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Vice General He Qing he pacified the various frontier rebellions and was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 初，守禮貶敘州，為僉事張文奎所辱。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouli was demoted to Xuzhou, he was humiliated by Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Wenkui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shouli was demoted to Xuzhou, he was humiliated by Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Wenkui.

sentences.zh: 至是，文奎遷四川參議，恐守禮修隙，先以所摭事奏。

translations.literal: At this time Wenkui was transferred to Sichuan as Participating Secretary; fearing Shouli would settle old scores, he first memorialized with collected accusations.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wenkui had been transferred to Sichuan as a participating secretary. Fearing that Shouli would settle old scores, he preemptively memorialized the throne with accusations he had gathered.

sentences.zh: 詔二人俱解職歸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered both men dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered both men dismissed from office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 守禮才器敏達，中外以為能。

translations.literal: Shouli was talented, capable, and quick; within and outside the court he was regarded as able.
translations.idiomatic: Shouli was talented, capable, and quick-witted, and was regarded as able both inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 居家未久，工部尚書秦金等會薦，起河南參政。

translations.literal: Not long at home, Minister of Works Qin Jin and others jointly recommended him; he was recalled as Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after returning home, Minister of Works Qin Jin and others jointly recommended him, and he was recalled to serve as Administration Vice Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 再遷右副都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 寇犯固原，為總督劉天和所敗。

translations.literal: Raiders invaded Guyuan and were defeated by Grand Coordinator Liu Tianhe.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders invaded Guyuan, they were defeated by Grand Coordinator Liu Tianhe.

sentences.zh: 欲自寧夏去，守禮與總兵任傑等邀敗之。

translations.literal: As they sought to leave Ningxia, Shouli together with Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie and others intercepted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: As the raiders tried to withdraw from Ningxia, Shouli together with Commander-in-Chief Ren Jie and others intercepted and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 會天和召還，進守禮右都御史總督軍務代之。

translations.literal: Just then Tianhe was recalled; Shouli was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right to take over general military affairs in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Tianhe was recalled to court, and Shouli was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right to take over general military affairs in his place.

sentences.zh: 錄前功，進兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His earlier merit was recorded and he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His earlier achievements were recognized, and he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 總兵官李義、楊信連卻吉囊，三賜璽書銀幣。

translations.literal: Commanders-in-Chief Li Yi and Yang Xin repeatedly repulsed Jinjang, and three times imperial sealed edicts with silver and silks were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-Chief Li Yi and Yang Xin repeatedly repulsed Jinjang, and on three occasions the court granted them imperial sealed edicts together with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏乞休，帝惡其避難，降俸二級。

translations.literal: Soon he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; the emperor, angered that he was avoiding hardship, reduced his salary by two grades.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial requesting retirement. The emperor, angered that he was trying to avoid hardship, reduced his salary by two grades.

sentences.zh: 其秋，寇三萬騎抵綏德。

translations.literal: That autumn, thirty thousand mounted raiders reached Suide.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, thirty thousand mounted raiders reached Suide.

sentences.zh: 遊擊張鵬卻之，總兵官吳英等追至塞外，東路參將周文兵亦至，夾擊敗之。

translations.literal: Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Peng repulsed them; Commander-in-Chief Wu Ying and others pursued beyond the border; Eastern Route Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Wen's troops also arrived; in a pincer attack they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps Commander Zhang Peng repulsed them; Commander-in-Chief Wu Ying and others pursued them beyond the border; troops under Eastern Route Assistant Regional Commander Zhou Wen also arrived, and in a pincer attack the raiders were defeated.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史殷學言，寇入內地五百里，請治諸將罪。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Yin Xue said the raiders had penetrated five hundred li into the interior and requested that the generals be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Censor Yin Xue argued that the raiders had penetrated five hundred li into the interior and requested that the generals be punished.

sentences.zh: 部議延綏遊兵俱調宣、大，寇方避實擊虛。

translations.literal: The ministry debated that the mobile troops of Yan-Sui had all been transferred to Xuan-Da; the raiders had been avoiding the strong and striking the weak.
